candidates.name: Chronic granulomatous disease
support_spans: Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils
candidates.why: The presence of a dense diffuse infiltrate of various immune cells, including histiocytes and giant cells, suggests a chronic granulomatous disease process.

candidates.name: Histoplasmosis
support_spans: Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
candidates.why: The finding of intracellular yeasts within histiocytes and giant cells is consistent with histoplasmosis, a fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum.

candidates.name: Oral histoplasmosis
support_spans: Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue with a clean base and irregular and elevated heaped-up margins
Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
candidates.why: The combination of a nonhealing oral ulcer and the presence of intracellular yeasts within histiocytes and giant cells on biopsy is consistent with oral histoplasmosis.

candidates.name: Histoplasmosis
support_spans: Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
Special stains (Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver nitrate and periodic acid–Schiff) highlighted fungal forms
candidates.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo and the highlighting of fungal forms by special stains are characteristic of Histoplasmosis.
